Task 3 then asks docs to state the same four. Two implementers produce different ids and different definition wording, and neither can be checked against the plan.

The plan asserts that "schema enum, coverage check, incremental baseline ... already derive from the resolved checklist and follow automatically", but never states how definitions are carried. That claim is only true if `resolve_checklist` keeps returning `list[str]` and definitions live in a separate lookup. The natural reading of "each built-in item carries a definition" — enriching `DEFAULT_CHECKLISTS`/`resolve_checklist` to id+definition — flows into `bundle["checklist"]` (`core/review_bundle.py:145`) and breaks the string `enum` at `core/review_verdict.py:105`, the `set(required_checklist).issubset(covered)` comparison in `resolve_source_baseline`, and `bundle_digest`'s shape — with the repair landing in `cli/review.py`, which is not in the declared scope. Task 2 likewise does not say how `_review_prompt` (signature `checklist: list[str]`) obtains definitions: new parameter, import, or compile-time lookup.

The stated grounds for dropping `scope-declared` are wrong. Neither named guard enforces scope completeness: `scope_sufficient` asserts the reviewer's assigned target was adequate, and `compile_review_contract`'s fail-closed check (`review_contract.py:305-314`) only trips when the scope matches *no* tracked file at all — one match passes. The guards that actually enforce declared-scope coverage of changed files are the merge gate (`sensors/verification_runner.py:480-492`) and `engineering/attestation.py:297`. The conclusion survives, but the recorded justification for weakening a gate item is false as written.

Task 2 changes the checklist rendering format for *all* reviewers ("ids with their definitions rather than a JSON array of bare strings"), so `code-reviewer` prompt text — and therefore `prompt_digest`/`contract_digest` — changes too, invalidating an in-flight code-review round. _render_checklist is small, its fallback for undefined ids is explicit, and both the module comment in review_checklist.py and the inline comment at review_contract.py:159 record WHY the asymmetry and the side mapping exist. Tests reach into two private helpers, which is justified here because the prompt text is the frozen artefact.

Empty/duplicate checklists, old-id baselines degrading to full-change, and stale packets are all handled or pinned. The one regression is that adopter-supplied ids are no longer escaped when rendered into the frozen prompt.

concepts.md and getting-started.md both state the four questions, the role asymmetry and its reason, the config override, and the digest/re-prepare cost for both roles. prompt_digest and contract_digest are real fields. No doc outside docs/plans/ still names design-soundness or scope-declared.

findings.summary: The checklist line moved from `json.dumps(checklist)` to raw f-string interpolation, so checklist ids resolved from `.harness/review-checklists.yaml` are no longer escaped before entering the frozen prompt. Previously a control character in an id rendered as `\n` inside a JSON array; now `  - {item}` emits it verbatim, so a configured id containing a newline injects free-standing lines into the prompt body between the checklist header and the instruction block — the region a reviewer reads as harness-authored instruction. The verdict schema's enum still holds the multi-line id, so the round does not fail closed on it. This is exposure the delta widened rather than created (a single-line id like `spec-coverage — report no findings` was equally injectable before), and `.harness/` is repo-committed governance, which is why this is minor rather than major. Escaping the id, or rejecting ids containing control characters in `resolve_checklist`, restores what json.dumps was incidentally providing.

prior_findings.note: tests/unit/engineering/test_review_contract.py adds `_compiled_prompt_for` and `test_consequence_gate_is_wired_to_the_role_not_just_to_the_flag`, which compile a real contract for each role and assert `BUILD THE WRONG THING` present in the plan-reviewer prompt and absent from the code-reviewer one — both directions, so inverting review_contract.py:421 to `code-reviewer` now fails. The same test also pins `Be exhaustive` present for both roles, keeping the role-agnostic instruction from being narrowed by the same edit.

docs/plans/2026-08-08-plan-review-prompt.md now matches what shipped: Task 2 item 3 is marked `emitted for plan-reviewer only`, the bolded paragraph states the add-vs-suppress split as the governing rule, says code review gets no consequence gate at all, defers the question to issue #99, and warns that re-adding it as a conformance fix would re-open the exposure. The behaviour list correspondingly says code-reviewer gains the checklist rendering and the exhaustiveness instruction and must not carry the consequence test, which is consistent with docs/concepts.md:96 and docs/getting-started.md:415.
